name: Left Atrial Appendage Aneurysm

criteria.description: Imaging evidence of localized aneurysmal dilation of the left atrial appendage
Presence of atrial arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation or flutter
History or evidence of systemic thromboembolism without other identifiable source
Exclusion of other causes of left atrial enlargement or aneurysm

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of left atrial appendage aneurysm plus exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities such as echocardiography, CT, or MRI.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized left atrial appendage aneurysmal dilation
pathognomonic.notes: Detected via imaging, considered pathognomonic anatomical feature
searchTerms: localized ballooning of left atrial appendage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Atrial arrhythmias originating from left atrial appendage
pathognomonic.notes: Includes atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter
searchTerms: irregular heartbeats from left atrial appendage
atrial arrhythmias starting in left atrium
abnormal heart rhythm from atrial pouch

occasional.symptomName: Chest discomfort or mild chest pain

occasional.notes: Due to arrhythmia or embolic events

searchTerms: feeling of skipped or fast heartbeats

occasional.notes: Rarely auscultated due to turbulent flow

rare.symptomName: Stroke with no other identifiable source
rare.notes: Embolic stroke secondary to thrombus formation

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; coagulation profile may be altered if thromboembolism present
imaging: Echocardiography showing localized aneurysmal dilation of left atrial appendage
Cardiac MRI or CT confirming aneurysm size and morphology
genetic: No known genetic mutations definitively linked; may be congenital or acquired
other: Electrophysiological studies may identify arrhythmogenic foci
Histopathology rarely performed; shows atrial wall thinning and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse left atrial dilation rather than localized appendage aneurysm
Often associated with mitral valve disease
Presence of thrombus without aneurysmal dilation
Usually secondary to atrial fibrillation or stasis
Extracardiac cystic mass adjacent to left atrium
No communication with left atrial appendage

redFlags: Sudden onset of neurological deficits suggestive of embolic stroke
New onset or worsening atrial arrhythmias
Signs of systemic embolism without other source
references: Aryal MR, Hakim FA, Ghimire S, et al. Left atrial appendage aneurysm: a systematic review of 82 cases. Echocardiography. 2014;31(10):1312-1318.
Kato TS, Kitamura M, Yamada T, et al. Left atrial appendage aneurysm: clinical features and surgical outcomes. Ann Thorac Surg. 2017;103(1):e1-e3.
Kawasaki M, Ohtsuka T, Matsumoto M, et al. Left atrial appendage aneurysm: a rare cause of embolic stroke. J Stroke Cerebrovasc Dis. 2019;28(2):e18-e20.
